sections.heading: Bogota-devnet-1 Status
sections.summary: Bogota-devnet-1 is running but RPC inconsistencies across clients hinder tooling and transaction receipt parsing.
sections.body:
- Bogota-devnet-1 has been launched and is running, though not under heavy stress yet; basic Frame transactions have been spammed on the network.
- Several bugs found in Panda tooling, particularly in spamoor, which has trouble maintaining consistent throughput on Frame transactions.
- Transaction receipts are inconsistent across clients, partly because the execution-APIs spec for Frame transactions is not yet finished and merged.
- Example inconsistency: the spec said `nonce` vs. `nonce_seq` for Frame transactions; most clients used `nonce`.
  - Geth, Nethermind and ethrex all backed `nonce` as the field name, but marc did not call it decided.
  - Besu abstained for now, citing a legacy-vs-new distinction that may be worth capturing in the nomenclature; marc left it as a fast-follow to resolve after the call.
  - Toni noted EIP-8250 may need a corresponding update.
- No spec tests have been run directly against the devnet yet; Stefan will look into doing so.
- No clients have implemented tracing APIs for Frame transactions; the block explorer (using `debug_traceBlockByHash` with the call tracer) gets no results for frames because a `frames` array is needed in the tracer output.
  - Action item: tracing API design for frames needs to be prioritized.

sections.heading: Next Devnet Planning and Scope
sections.summary: Working plan is a bogota-devnet-2 (EL-only); client teams will bring their scope preferences to Thursday's ACD call.
sections.body:
- Whether to combine EL and CL into a merged "hegota" devnet was raised but not settled; that decision is deferred to the next ACDT.
- Agreement to proceed with a bogota-devnet-2 (EL-only) in the meantime, targeting launch later next week before teams travel to Mumbai.
- lightclient noted that RPC and tracing formats are still unsettled, so adding too many new EIPs could dilute focus on those.
- Spencer (EEST) proposed adding five additional EIPs to the next devnet:
  - [EIP-4758](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4758) Deactivate SELFDESTRUCT — reduces test space.
  - EIP-8298 SETCODEFROM — critical PQ-transition component.
  - EIP-8253 Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts — requires fork transition testing.
  - EIP-8131 Unified Transaction Content Floor — enables earlier benchmarking.
  - EIP-8279 Block Access List Byte Floor — enables earlier benchmarking.
- lightclient called SETCODEFROM and EIP-8151 pretty critical PQ-transition parts; ethrex proposed exactly that pair, with Nethermind and others agreeing in chat.
- soispoke requested testing multiple concurrent private transactions per sender with MATCHA, to exercise mempool subtleties and attack resilience.
- spencer flagged that agreeing EIPs in this breakout may bypass process; lightclient agreed formal agreement should happen at ACD/ACDT.
- Action item: each client team to bring a list of what they are comfortable including in bogota-devnet-2 to Thursday's ACD call.

sections.heading: Max Fee PR (EIP-8141, PR 12414)
sections.summary: Broad tentative support for including the max_fee aggregate-cost field on devnet-2; lightclient will address open questions and check for objections at ACD Thursday.
sections.body:
- The max fee concept originates from [EIP-7999](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7999) (multidimensional fee market) and is proposed as a [PR to EIP-8141](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12414).
- It introduces a single `max_fee` field covering all gas dimensions (execution, state, blobs) instead of per-dimension priority and max fees.
- lightclient emphasized this is an accounting technique, not a full multidimensional market change — no new base fees are introduced.
- Gas dimension limits remain rigid under the current spec; no cross-bucket "spilling" from one dimension to another.
- soispoke raised concern that multidimensional fee EIPs historically carry hidden complexity and questioned whether shipping it as a PR within frames is premature.
- lightclient argued the change is reversible on future devnets if problems emerge, and Anders has vetted the design and sees no unresolved complexity.
- Besu (Justin Florentine) expressed partial opposition on design grounds — prefers full EIP-7999 treatment — but acknowledged the PR is a net simplification and would not block it.
  - Florentine offered to explore a competing PR that excises gas accounting from 8141 entirely, relying on 7999 or status-quo EIP-8037.
  - lightclient pushed back: EIP-8037's state gas reservoir is a backwards-compatible hack for 1D transactions; a new tx object should expose the state gas field natively.
- Daniil (Nethermind) left a comment on the PR about banning fee-access opcodes vs. reading max_fee inside verify frame; lightclient needs to think through the sponsoring flow before resolving.
- ethrex and Nethermind both supportive of trying it on devnet.
- Plan: lightclient to resolve Daniil's question, rebase the PR, and raise it again at Thursday's ACD for final objections before merging.

sections.heading: Signature Length Bounding PR (EIP-8141, PR 12502)
sections.summary: PR to hash arbitrary signature lengths into the canonical signature hash will be merged; no objections raised.
sections.body:
- Problem: arbitrary-length signature objects in the signature list are dynamically sized and charged proportionally for calldata, but the signature data is not included in the canonical signature hash, making it malleable.
- A relayer could pad signature data (e.g., add a kilobyte of junk), inflating cost charged to the user without their consent.
- Fix ([PR 12502](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12502) to EIP-8141): the length of each arbitrary signature object is hashed into the canonical signature hash, bounding the potential cost impact of malleability.
- Worst case after the fix: a relayer can still alter signature validity (inherent trade-off of excluding data from the canonical hash), but cannot inflate user costs.
- lightclient described this as a critical update; no objections were raised.
- Decision: lightclient will merge the PR after the call; it will be included in the next devnet.

sections.heading: TXDIFF Opcode Removal Proposal (EIP-7906, PR 12530)
sections.summary: Proposal to remove TXDIFF in favor of TXTRACE alone is tabled; pre-state slot reads (e.g., proxy front-run protection) remain an unresolved use case.
sections.body:
- lightclient proposed removing the TXDIFF opcode from EIP-7906 ([PR 12530](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12530)), arguing that TXTRACE (iterating all transaction changes) covers most use cases and TXDIFF is an optimization.
- The PR adds nonce-change information back into TXTRACE to compensate.
- Alex Forshtat (approved the PR but) raised a key counter-argument: TXDIFF enables querying pre-state values that were unchanged within the transaction.
  - Use case: clear signing against proxy contracts — a user may want to assert the implementation slot value at transaction start to guard against front-run proxy upgrades.
  - If the slot was not modified within the transaction, TXTRACE would not surface it.
- lightclient acknowledged this as a valid gap and will think further before rebasing the PR to allow auto-merge.
- The EIP bot auto-merged the PR during the call despite lightclient's intent to hold; lightclient will continue evaluating.
- Decision deferred to a future call.

sections.heading: VERIFY_NONSTATE / VERIFY_STATE Frame Separation (OCL Proposal)
sections.summary: OCL proposed splitting verify frame into stateless and stateful modes to save L2 sequencers redundant verification; discussion deferred to async.
sections.body:
- Justin Zen (OCL) proposed splitting the verify frame into VERIFY_NONSTATE (heavy computation like signature verification) and VERIFY_STATE (state checks like recovered-address lookup).
  - Motivation: L2 sequencers could skip re-executing the stateless portion if the state hasn't changed, saving computation.
- lightclient questioned how this differs from the existing signature list mechanism, where protocol-known signatures are verified statelessly outside frame execution, and arbitrary schemes use the frame destination as an allow list.
  - The only trade-off is that arbitrary stateless schemes are not fully permissionless under the current design.
- Justin Zen had connectivity issues and could not fully respond.
- Related ERC PR shared: [ERCs PR #1738](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/pull/1738).
- Discussion to continue asynchronously.
